findings.issue: The review target containment check compares scope paths against the raw reviewTarget text. A files target written as a glob is in contract: deep-review.yaml lines 793-797 say 'Expand glob patterns from review_target', and the expanded list is stored as reviewScopeFiles (yaml line 874). Containment only consults that list for commit ranges (line 405), so with a glob target like 'src/**/*.ts' no scope path equals the target or starts with it plus '/'. Every seed and admission proposal that carries a path scope is pruned as 'relevance'. seedNodes returns admitted: [] with no warning, and the expansive review runs at its loop default with an empty frontier. A '.' target prunes the same way, while a './' target normalizes to blank and allows every scope. Fix: when the target is a pattern or names the repo root, test containment against reviewScopeFiles through scopeInsideTouchedFiles, as commit ranges already do. Keep the change on the target side: mapping '.' to blank in the shared normalizer would break the new test asserting that scope '.' is outside the target.

evidence.cmd: node -e 'seedNodes({artifactDir, target:"review", candidates:[{question:"Does a.ts leak a handle?",scope:"src/a.ts"},{question:"Does b.ts race?",scope:["src/b.ts"]}]})' with review config {reviewTargetType:"files",reviewTarget:"src/**/*.ts",reviewScopeFiles:["src/a.ts","src/b.ts"]}; plus scopeInsideReviewTarget probes
evidence.out: {"admitted":0,"pruned":["relevance","relevance"]}; glob false, dot false, dotslash true; all-pruned seed result: {"admitted":[],"pruned":[{"nodeId":"F-1-001","reason":"relevance"}],"derivedMaxIterations":7,"growthSlots":3} with no warning field
